<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 47a3b95ecc3960b3d57d2dfe9f082293096df9a3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a71698527b303c8c2f5b00b92134ebb43157bbd9` — the merge of head `7b27d05a6c7380c5508756ba2d67c8fca099636a` into base `47a3b95ecc3960b3d57d2dfe9f082293096df9a3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a71698527b303c8c2f5b00b92134ebb43157bbd9 && git checkout a71698527b303c8c2f5b00b92134ebb43157bbd9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 47a3b95ecc3960b3d57d2dfe9f082293096df9a3 7b27d05a6c7380c5508756ba2d67c8fca099636a && git checkout -B drift-repro 47a3b95ecc3960b3d57d2dfe9f082293096df9a3 && git merge --no-ff 7b27d05a6c7380c5508756ba2d67c8fca099636a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 47a3b95ecc3960b3d57d2dfe9f082293096df9a3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 47a3b95ecc3960b3d57d2dfe9f082293096df9a3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7b27d05a6c7380c5508756ba2d67c8fca099636a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-delegation.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-delegation-inert-shapes.integration.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/translations/*.objects.generated.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/translations/*.source-hashes.generated.ts, .changeset/33062-delegation-inert-shapes.md + packages/core/src/security/grant-validity.ts (`isGrantActive`) (read, not reviewed)

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the changeset). Diff read against merge base `e540baf8`.

### ① Derived judgments

- `validity_window_order` refuses `valid_until <= valid_from` with both bounds set. That is exactly the set `isGrantActive` can never make active: it admits `valid_from <= now < valid_until`, which is empty when `until <= from`, so refusing equal bounds is right. Both fields are `Field.datetime`, so `datetime()` compares instants, not spellings. Either bound empty is not judged (open-ended window kept).
- `delegate_not_delegator` refuses `delegate_id == delegator_id` with a delegate set. Declared rules run after the `beforeInsert` hooks, so a delegator stamped by `bindDelegationWriteGuard` is judged too (pinned: "leaves the delegator to the write guard's stamp").
- The `previous == null || <compared column moved>` guard limits each rule to inserts and to updates that move a compared column, so a row stored inert before this release still takes unrelated edits, and the write that repairs it must state a valid value. Pinned both ways. A moved-but-still-inert update is refused, which is the intended reading.
- Both rules are `cross_field` with the violated field first, so `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` attaches to `valid_until` / `delegate_id`. The test checks status, field and that nothing is stored, for the delegator and for a system writer. Controls: valid window and delegate, open-ended windows, a bound moved within a valid window.
- Translations: en and zh-CN carry real text. The other nine locales carry the English text with a `source-hashes` entry, which is the generator's marker for "byte copy of the source, not translated". That is the repo's mechanism for untranslated leaves, so they surface as untranslated rather than passing as translated.
- Checks on this head: 38 success, 15 skipped, none failed; mergeable clean.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-approvals` `patch` with the BREAKING banner via `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Right: two declared validation rules on a platform object's rows move no authorable key, value or type, and an inert row needs no rewrite.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No published schema (`packages/spec/src/**`) and no governed path in the diff. The `P` tag and the `previous` binding are existing spec surfaces, used the same way as `sys_user_permission_set.validity_window_order`.
- Nit (does not block): the zh-Hant and the other non-zh locales show the English message until translated. Tracked by the source-hash entries; no change needed here.

### ④ Design judgment

Against `approvals.mdx` and ADR-0091 on `main`: a delegation applies from `valid_from` up to `valid_until`, and it reroutes a slot to another user. Neither refused shape can ever do that, and storing them with `201` misled the delegator into thinking their approvals were covered. Refusing them at the write, naming the field, is the right fix. Declaring the rules on the object (rather than a hook) puts them on every write path, and the `previous` guard keeps the narrowing to writes that create the shape, so no existing row is locked. The docs paragraph says what is refused, how to make an open-ended window, and what to do with an old inert row. No must-fix or should-fix.
